title: Bass drum mutes and the ringing sound
summary: Cloths replaced by mutes to stop ringing; Frazier demonstrates, saying old bands liked a ringing bass drum; Allen asks about crowfoot pedals.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: When did they start putting the dampers on these drums? Did they always have them on there?

No, we first started with cloths, using cloths on the bass drums. They killed the ringing sound effect of it when the band started improving. And now, well, I forgot what year these mutes came out. I really forgot what, but I know it's a pretty good ways back.
What exactly what you can't remember.
Is it, you think it spoils a tone on there?

No, no, it helps with a whole lot. It stops the drum from ringing a whole lot. You see, without that mute, here's a fake. You get, of course, this drum is still, I have that patent on it. But I'll give you a little idea, without that mute, with the sound, you see, with that patent. You know, just in the sound. And I still have a patent on there with that ball hitting on there.
Can we just put the mute on again and see how it sounds?

Tighten it up a little more, you see. All right, that's good right there. Okay. Okay. Keep that ringing effect off. Now, years ago, the drum couldn't ring enough. The more it'd ring, the more the band would like it.
The more they'd like it, yeah.
Big, that booming sound, didn't it?
Yeah, yeah. Let a bass drum ring, it goes right to the band's hand, you see, you could hear it from them. Good ways off.
You know, what are those things they call crowfoot pedals? You remember them? Crowfoot pedals? Yeah.
